title: bonsai.now/1
description: bonsai now --json (contract §23; plan P-T-5795 step 2 and its Amendment 2): the time now, as Bonsai's clock gives it, in the form every record takes (UTC) and, for a person, in the local zone, so an agent copies a time instead of guessing one. Printed, never stored. Written by bonsai now with --json; read by agents and the hook line that tells them the time. On a refusal every field but format and error is null. A writer writes every field below, in this order, null where it does not apply (contract §2.2); a reader treats a missing field as null, keeps an unknown one and refuses a duplicate key.

format.description: The version, always the first field (contract §2.2).

utc.description: The time now in UTC, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM: the record form, what a run report's started and finished hold (contract §23); null on a refusal.

day.description: The UTC day, YYYY-MM-DD: what a task's created, started and finished and STATE's and a memory note's updated hold (contract §23); null on a refusal.

iso.description: The same instant, ISO-8601 UTC with milliseconds and Z: the form of the log's at and a message's created (contract §23); null on a refusal.

local.description: The same instant in the local zone with its offset, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM +HH:MM: the display form, for a person to read, never recorded (contract §23); null on a refusal.

offset.description: The local zone's offset from UTC now, +HH:MM or -HH:MM, the one local shows; for display only (contract §23); null on a refusal.

zone.description: The local zone's abbreviation as Go prints it (IST, CEST; +0530 where the zone has none), for a person's eye only: never parsed and never recorded, since one abbreviation can name more than one zone (contract §23). null on a refusal.

error.description: null unless the command refused or failed: then what went wrong and the next step, as bonsai.error has it.

examples.message: bonsai.yaml is not in this checkout, so it is not linked to Bonsai

next.do: run: bonsai init in the project's main checkout

code.description: What went wrong, as a fixed word: an open list (contract §2.2). Later steps add words, which is an addition (format review 4.5), and a reader shows a word it does not know as other. The known words live in one table in Bonsai's code, their one home, which bonsai check --schema bonsai.error prints (and, from step 5.1.10, the reference page of lists, docs/reference/lists.md); this schema does not copy them, and the words in its examples are illustrative.

message.description: What is wrong, one sentence for a person, in ASCII (spec §3).
examples: no --yes, and no terminal to ask at: nothing was written

next.description: The next thing to do (spec §3: every refusal and error names it, in the human line and in the JSON): what to do and who does it.

do.description: What to do: the command to run, written run: and the command line, or the step in plain words.
examples: open Claude Code in this checkout and accept its trust question

who.description: Who does it, a closed list: agent (any agent may do it, unattended) or person (a person's step: a consent such as --allow-exec, a tap, a setting, an install, or a command an agent's task does not grant it; spec §4, §6).
